answer: A reputation is like a meadow that turns green only after a season of rain. A new identity starts with an empty vault and earns nothing until it has banked twenty reviewed tasks. Every epoch the system re-audits three random entries per vault; one failed audit freezes that vault for ten epochs. Each task carries a pigment stamp, a hash of the task, reviewers and epoch seed, so a copied stamp is caught at once, each account losing fifty credits. Faking a hundred identities would cost two thousand hours of reviewed work and five thousand credits.
